## Outcomes

Source: your partner's words, 2026-11-06. Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md, specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md.
Choices made: Python 3.14 in the existing uv workspace of four scaffolded packages (repo scaffold).

| # | Outcome | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | The quarterly and daily index files, ingested into one filing-index table | A | 1 | Small: about 130 quarterly files since 1993 plus one daily file per business day, so minutes of downloading at 3 requests/second; from the SEC full-index and daily-index directories |
| O2 | The individual submissions that the index rows name, downloaded | A | 2 | Large: millions of files, so weeks of downloading for the full history at 3 requests/second; from index row count × request rate, not yet measured (measured by Stage 2) |
| O3 | 10-K and 8-K filings handled: picked out of the submissions, with their main documents extracted | A | 3 | Unknown until submissions are on disk (measured by Stage 3) |

Tracks: A — SEC filing ingestion (known progression).

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Filing-index core
      Objective: Build one filing-index table from one real closed quarter's quarterly index and that quarter's daily indexes.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: nothing (package scaffolds only)
      Produces: the filing-index table for that quarter; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O1: the table holds one row per filing for the quarter, built from both the quarterly and daily files, and can be queried. The findings file records the bytes downloaded, the request count, the row count and the elapsed time of the real run.
      Leaves out: raw replay, source manifest, checkpoint/resume, historical-format fixtures (Stage 4); full index history, daily catch-up (Stage 5); reconciliation, versioned publication (Stage 6); scheduling, deployment (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Submissions core
      Objective: Download the submissions that a bounded real slice of Stage 1's table names.
      Outcomes: O2
      Consumes: Stage 1's filing-index table
      Produces: the slice's submissions on disk, keyed to their index rows; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-2-findings.md
      Exit: O2: every row in the slice either has its submission on disk or is reported as failed with a reason. The findings file records the measured time and bytes per submission, and the full-history estimate projected from those figures.
      Leaves out: full submissions history, submissions checkpoint/resume, shared request budget (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 3: 10-K and 8-K core
      Objective: Pick the 10-K and 8-K filings out of Stage 2's submissions and extract their main documents.
      Outcomes: O3
      Consumes: Stage 2's submissions on disk
      Produces: extracted main documents for the slice's 10-K and 8-K filings; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-3-findings.md
      Exit: O3: each 10-K and 8-K in the slice has its main document extracted or is reported as having no identifiable main document. The findings file records the counts and the elapsed time.
      Leaves out: 10-K/8-K over full history, document-format fixtures (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 4: Index durability
      Objective: Make index ingestion replayable from retained raw bytes, traceable to its sources, and resumable after failure.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: Stage 1's index ingestion and findings
      Produces: raw replay, source manifest, checkpoint/resume, historical-format fixtures for index files
      Exit: O1: rebuilding the Stage 1 table from retained raw bytes makes no SEC requests and produces the same rows. Every row traces to a source file and its hash. An interrupted run resumes without redoing completed files.
      Leaves out: full index history, daily catch-up (Stage 5)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 5: Full index history and daily catch-up
      Objective: Extend the table to the full historical range and keep it current from the daily indexes, including after missed runs.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: Stage 4's raw replay, source manifest, checkpoint/resume, historical-format fixtures
      Produces: full index history in the filing-index table; daily catch-up
      Exit: O1: the table covers every quarter in the chosen range, with unresolved gaps listed by file. A catch-up run after a simulated multi-day outage fills the missed days without duplicate rows.
      Leaves out: reconciliation, versioned publication (Stage 6); scheduling, deployment (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 6: Index reconciliation and versioned publication
      Objective: Re-read quarterly indexes, record SEC-side changes over time, and publish the table so readers never see a partial update.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: Stage 5's full index history; Stage 4's source manifest
      Produces: reconciliation, versioned publication
      Exit: O1: a reconciliation run over a changed quarterly fixture records each added, changed and removed row against its source. Readers of the published table see either the previous version or the new one, never a mix.
      Leaves out: scheduling, deployment (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 7: Full submissions history and 10-K/8-K at scale
      Objective: Download the submissions for the full index history and handle every 10-K and 8-K in them.
      Outcomes: O2, O3
      Consumes: Stage 5's full index history; Stage 2's and Stage 3's code and findings; Stage 4's checkpoint/resume
      Produces: full submissions history, submissions checkpoint/resume, shared request budget, 10-K/8-K over full history, document-format fixtures
      Exit: O2: every index row in the chosen range either has its submission on disk or is listed as pending or failed, and an interrupted run resumes without re-downloading. All SEC collectors running at once stay within one request budget. O3: every 10-K and 8-K in the range is extracted or reported, and the document-format fixtures pass.
      Leaves out: scheduling, deployment (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 8: Scheduling and deployment
      Objective: Run daily ingestion, reconciliation and submissions collection unattended on a chosen platform, with monitoring and runbooks.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3
      Consumes: Stage 5's daily catch-up; Stage 6's reconciliation, versioned publication; Stage 7's shared request budget
      Produces: scheduling, deployment
      Exit: O1, O2 and O3: an observed scheduled run of each job completes, and its durable report and alerts can be inspected. A runbook covers each recovery path, and the rollback procedure has been exercised.
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: brainstorming
